changes: Removed 'Mamdevyalī' as scribe: the line is an anuṣṭubh half-verse ('tāropākhyamaṇirāma- / ṣyaṣyāṃ maṃdevy alīlikhat'), and '-lī likhat' is the verb alīlikhat, not part of a name
Maṇirāma: role changed from owner to commissioner (alīlikhat, a causative aorist: 'had [this] written'), noting he may be the scribe; 'tāropākhya' moved from titles to affiliation as the surname Tāro
Śaṅkara: role changed from teacher to other (he is the author's teacher, not connected with this copy); name normalised to Śaṅkara
Author name changed from Sudeśvarācārya to Sureśvara, with 'ācārya' as a title only; the corruption is noted
Removed the wrote_for relation, which depended on the false scribe
Notes rewritten with the metrical analysis and the uncertainty about the era

date.as_written: vasu vāṇavasu kṣoṇī mita varṣe nabhasyamuṃ

notes: The chronogram vasu (8), bāṇa (5), vasu (8), kṣoṇī (1), read right to left, gives 1858. No era is named. If it is VS, the year is about 1801 CE, which fits a Devanagari manuscript with the name Maṇirāma; if it is ŚS, it would be about 1936 CE. Nabhasya is Bhādrapada; 'nabhasy amum' means 'in Nabhasya, this [book]'. The dating line is an anuṣṭubh: 'vasubāṇavasukṣoṇī-mitavarṣe nabhasy amum | tāropākhyamaṇirāma-ṣyaṣyāṃ(?)maṃdevy alīlikhat'. The verb is alīlikhat, a causative aorist ('had written'), though it is often used loosely for 'wrote', so Maṇirāma may be the scribe rather than the commissioner. 'ṣyaṣyāṃ(!) maṃdevy' is corrupt (the cataloguer marked it with '!') and may hide a further word, such as a form of śiṣya or a female name ending in -devī, but no reliable name can be recovered from it. Śaṅkara is named only as the author's teacher. 'Sudeśvara' is a corruption of Sureśvara.
